title: Audit interior dependencies behind Reddy and Knight’s character prediction result
statement: Repeat the character prediction assay across independently fixed symbol inventories and type-disjoint reference-word sets. Compare bag-of-letters and edge-preserving controls. Establish how much above their predictions survives rebundling EVA multicharacter sequences, and test the identical assay on alphabetic and consonantal reference texts.
check: Report micro-averaged unigram and previous-character top-one accuracy with the support, token type selection, first-character convention and rule for duplicates declared. Fit each null model on the independently shuffled training words and measure its matching test words. Keep source word bags and lengths fixed in both nulls.
source: Sravana Reddy and Kevin Knight (2011), What We Know About the Voynich Manuscript, §4.2, Table 2, https://aclanthology.org/W11-1511/ .
pilot: Public practice only. Restrict to certain P words in Currier B and the declared plain-EVA alphabet. Fit on one copy of every eligible type on public nonpractice faces. Score only practice types absent from that fit. Break ties lexicographically and use a distinct start symbol for bigrams. Shuffle each word independently (all symbols, or interior only) with 16 fixed seeds and retain the original type rows, even if scrambled strings coincide. The test uses both ZL and IT as alternate transcriptions of the same codex.
findings: ZL train/test types 4,260/487. Top-one unigram and bigram 10.83% and 36.57%. Full and edge-fixed shuffle median bigram 14.55% and 15.97%. IT 4,308/481 and accuracies 10.71% and 36.19%, with shuffle medians 14.45%/16.38%. This extends the previous-context result to type-disjoint plain-EVA public data. The edge-fixed null retains roughly one fifth of the original unigram-to-bigram gain. Interior ordering explains much of the remaining gain relative to these controls. This pilot does not compare to reference languages or distinguish encoding, glyph conventions and other production choices. It differs from the paper’s word-type cross-validation and symbol representation.
